title: A living ocean in motion
explain: The model would track temperature, salinity, currents, nutrients and oxygen alongside plankton and benthic communities. Mixing, transport, growth and carbon cycling connect those states across depths and timescales.
test: Anchor each measurement to a region, depth, time and instrument. Use observations withheld by event or dive to test what the model predicts.

title: Wind stirs the surface layer
explain: Wind inputs energy at the surface. When turbulence overcomes stratification, water from different depths mixes and redistributes heat, salt and nutrients.
test: Compare wind with temperature and salinity profiles through the storm. A single depth cannot establish how far mixing reached.

title: Currents carry water and particles
explain: A current can carry fresher water and its particle community past a fixed mooring. A rise in particle counts can therefore occur even without local growth.
test: Compare upstream salinity and particle records with current speed and direction. Look for a lag consistent with travel between stations.

title: Light and nutrients support a food web
explain: Phytoplankton use light and dissolved nutrients to grow. Grazers consume some of that production. Growth, grazing and transport can all change the particles in a water sample.
test: Compare light and nutrient profiles with expert-reviewed plankton imagery. Fluorescence and total image-region counts alone cannot separate growth from grazing.

title: Sinking particles carry carbon downward
explain: Organic material can aggregate into marine snow. Some is consumed or decomposed as it sinks, and a fraction reaches the seafloor. The flux changes with depth.
test: Pair particle imagery with depth-resolved sediment traps in the same region. Surface image counts alone cannot quantify sinking carbon flux.

title: Food and oxygen shape benthic habitat
explain: Sinking material can supply food to benthic animals. Near-bottom oxygen and substrate help determine which animals can live there. Cameras sample the visible community.
test: Pair repeat transects with oxygen, substrate and surveyed area. The V4277 benchmark tells us how often detectors found annotated animals on one dive.
